title: CAN LLMS KEEP A SECRET? TESTING PRIVACY IMPLICATIONS OF LANGUAGE MODELS VIA CONTEXTUAL INTEGRITY THEORY
reasoning: The paper benchmarks LLMs on their ability to reason about privacy using 'contextual integrity' theory, which includes evaluating how models handle 'religion' and 'religious and spiritual views' as sensitive information. It also incorporates 'moral incentives' based on Schwartz's theory of basic values to test secret-sharing behavior and discusses the 'moral legitimacy' and 'normative judgments' associated with information flows.
